title: What does Houthi advance mean for Yemen’s southern separatists?
gist: Houthi forces have taken Mayyun Island and the Red Sea port of Mokha, and Al-Monitor reports that the anti-Houthi coalition is too fractured to mount a counteroffensive because the Saudi-UAE rift gutted the Southern Transitional Council, whose remaining force is in the low thousands; analysts expect the Houthis to use Bab al-Mandeb the way Iran uses Hormuz.

themes.theme: Chokepoint capture and the Hormuz playbook

insights.claim: The Houthis captured Mayyun Island on Friday, giving them control of the strategic Bab al-Mandeb strait area along the Red Sea, after seizing the Red Sea port city of Mokha on Thursday.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Two chokepoint assets taken in 48 hours means Red Sea transit risk is now a function of Houthi policy, not just missile range.
insights.locator: The Houthis captured Mayyun Island on Friday

insights.claim: Former Yemeni foreign minister Khaled Alyemany predicts the Houthis' next step is closing Bab al-Mandeb and using the same tactics as in Hormuz, implying transit denial or fee extraction rather than sporadic attacks.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: If both Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb operate under coercive transit regimes, seaborne energy and container routes face a structural, not cyclical, cost increase.
insights.quote: The next step is closing it and using the same tactics as in Hormuz.

insights.claim: Alyemany argues the Houthi gains were no surprise but the product of accumulated political and military failure, and that the group was left unattended until Tehran instructed it to take Bab al-Mandeb.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Framing the advance as Tehran-directed means Bab al-Mandeb is a bargaining chip in US-Iran negotiations, so the strait's status tracks the nuclear and sanctions file.
insights.quote: The Houthis were left unattended until they received instructions from Tehran to take Bab al-Mandeb
insights.locator: Ambassador Khaled Alyemany, a US-based adviser

insights.claim: The Yemeni government's armed forces began striking Houthi positions in southwest Yemen including near Mokha, indicating contested rather than consolidated Houthi control of the coast.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Active counter-strikes near Mokha keep the port's usability uncertain, sustaining insurance premiums even if the Houthis nominally hold it.
insights.locator: The Yemeni government's armed forces said later on Friday

themes.theme: The Saudi-UAE rift as root cause

insights.claim: The anti-Houthi coalition has been severely weakened by Saudi-UAE tensions over south Yemen, making a counteroffensive difficult, according to a Yemeni expert cited by Al-Monitor.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: The binding constraint on rolling back Houthi gains is Gulf disunity, not firepower, so watch Riyadh-Abu Dhabi relations as the leading indicator for Red Sea security.
insights.locator: One Yemeni expert said that the anti-Houthi coalition has been severely weakened

insights.claim: Mohammed al-Basha of the Basha Report says the UAE-Saudi spat weakened the anti-Houthi coalition from the core, and that before the breakup the STC would have joined northern forces to expel the Houthis from specific locations - cooperation that will not happen today.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: The loss of north-south battlefield cooperation removes the only mechanism that previously reversed Houthi advances, so expect gains to stick.
insights.quote: Before the UAE-Saudi breakup, the STC would’ve joined forces with northern forces to expel Houthis from certain locations, but we won’t see that today

insights.claim: Saudi-UAE divergence extends beyond Yemen: the UAE has economic interests in the breakaway state Somaliland and allegedly supports Sudan's Rapid Support Forces, while Saudi Arabia is close to the Sudanese armed forces and the Somali government.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Treat Yemen, Sudan and the Horn of Africa as one correlated Saudi-UAE rivalry theater; escalation in one raises proxy risk across Red Sea logistics corridors.
insights.locator: Both countries are seeking regional influence

insights.claim: The December 2025 STC offensive against government forces, reversed by mid-January with Saudi air power, stemmed from UAE support for southern separatism clashing with Saudi efforts to reach a peace deal with the Houthis.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Riyadh's preference for a Houthi peace deal over defeating them explains why Saudi escalation against the Houthis has limits even after strikes on its own territory.
insights.locator: The UAE's support for southern separatism contrasted

themes.theme: What is left of the STC

insights.claim: Al-Basha estimates the Southern Transitional Council's remaining force at 'low thousands', based in southwest Al-Dhale province north of Aden with residual presence in Aden and Hadhramaut.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: A low-thousands force cannot alter the military balance, so any plan that counts on southern separatists to contain the Houthis is not credible.
insights.quote: Whatever remaining force they have is in the low thousands

insights.claim: Members of the STC announced the group's dissolution from Riyadh in January, but other council members reject that and figures associated with the body say it remains active - so the STC is contested rather than defunct.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: An ambiguous legal and organizational status makes the STC an unreliable counterparty for any US or Gulf-brokered coalition arrangement.
insights.locator: Members of the STC announced the group's dissolution from Riyadh

insights.claim: Former STC leader Aidarus al-Zubaidi is in exile in the UAE and a number of members have resigned or joined other armed groups, confirming leadership decapitation and fragmentation.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Exiled leadership means the UAE retains a dormant southern card it could reactivate if it chooses to re-enter Yemen.
insights.locator: Former STC leader Aidarus al-Zubaidi is currently in exile

insights.claim: The STC is internally divided on the Houthi advance, with some members using social media to deter action against the Houthis out of anger toward Saudi Arabia while others see any Houthi move toward the south or western coast as an existential threat.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Anti-Saudi resentment is strong enough inside the southern camp to produce de facto acquiescence to Houthi gains, further reducing counteroffensive odds.
insights.quote: Other STC members…view any Houthi advance toward the south or the western coastline of Yemen as an existential threat
insights.locator: One southern Yemeni source familiar with the situation

insights.claim: A southern Yemeni source says STC figures read the Houthi advances as definitive proof that northern-dominated government forces are infiltrated by Houthi operatives and cannot hold territory.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: If southern actors believe government forces are compromised, intelligence sharing and joint operations become politically impossible, entrenching the split.
insights.quote: Politically, they see these advances as definitive proof that northern-dominated government forces are infiltrated by Houthi operatives and cannot hold territory.
insights.locator: One southern Yemeni source familiar with the situation

insights.claim: Al-Basha says the Houthis have been very careful in dealing with the south and have not moved into the southwestern tip of Yemen that was part of former South Yemen, issuing statements that they are not trying to occupy the south.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Deliberate Houthi restraint caps the near-term escalation scenario in Aden and Hadhramaut, where most southern oil and port assets sit.
insights.quote: They’ve issued statements saying they are not trying to occupy the south. They’re probably trying to pressure the south into a (new) structure
insights.locator: Basha described the Houthis as being "very careful"

insights.claim: Al-Basha frames Houthi restraint as practical arithmetic rather than moderation: they have no base of support in the south, it would be a tough battle and they cannot kill their way through the whole country, but he expects them to push ahead eventually if they do not get what they want.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Restraint is conditional and transactional, so a failed negotiation - not a new offensive decision - is the trigger to watch for a southern escalation.
insights.quote: They know they have no base of support in the south. They know it’s going to be a tough battle and they can’t kill their way through the whole country
insights.locator: Basha said the Houthi reluctance to move

insights.claim: The Houthis are probably trying to pressure the south into a new political structure rather than occupy it, meaning their military gains are instruments of a governance negotiation.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: If the endgame is a negotiated national structure, the Houthis have an incentive to keep shipping leverage alive until that deal is struck.
insights.locator: They're probably trying to pressure the south into a (new) structure

insights.claim: The Institute for the Study of War identifies the National Shield Forces, the Southern Giants Brigades and the National Resistance Forces as the main targets of the Houthi offensive in southwest Taiz province and in Hadhramaut.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
entities: Institute for the Study of War
insights.so_what: These three militias, not the regular army, are the actual line of defense for Yemen's coast; their attrition rate is the metric that forecasts further Houthi gains.
insights.locator: The Washington-based Institute for the Study of War identified

insights.claim: The National Resistance Forces are led by Tareq Saleh, nephew of former President Ali Abdullah Saleh, while the Southern Giants Brigades were previously UAE-backed but now cooperate with the government and the National Shield Forces were formed by the Presidential Leadership Council.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: The anti-Houthi order of battle is a patchwork of personality- and patron-based militias, which explains why command unity and a coordinated counteroffensive remain out of reach.
insights.locator: The National Shield Forces were formed by the government's

insights.claim: Alyemany says the STC wanted to help counter the Houthis in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden but that the Saudi-backed coalition 'sees the STC as an enemy', and he appeals for American leadership to bring all components together.
insights.speaker: Adam Lucente
insights.so_what: Southern actors are lobbying the Trump administration directly, so US recognition of the STC would be an early signal of a re-engineered anti-Houthi coalition.
insights.quote: American leadership should bring all components together
insights.locator: Alyemany said that the STC had expressed a desire
